This finding, known as a hydropneumothorax, means there is both air and fluid trapped between the lung and the chest wall, which can happen after surgery, trauma, or infection. Because of this collection, the left lung appears smaller than normal, as it is being compressed. The right lung shows some mild haziness, which could be due to mild fluid buildup or old scarring, though it is less specific. There are also surgical clips near the neck, suggesting the patient has had prior neck surgery, such as removal of the thyroid gland. Overall, the main concern is the large air-fluid collection in the left chest, which usually requires further evaluation (such as a CT scan) and likely drainage or treatment depending on the underlying cause.
